title: New Minami-ke Korekara TV Anime's Teaser Unveils Cast, Staff, April Debut
content:
The " Minami-ke Special Event 2026" debuted the teaser promotional video, teaser visual, and character visuals for Minami-ke: Korekara ( Minami-ke : Going Forward), the new sequel television anime series based on Coharu Sakuraba 's Minami-ke manga , on Sunday. The teaser video announces the new series' returning cast, staff, and April 2027 premiere.

The returning cast members are:

• Rina Satō as Haruka Minami

• Marina Inoue as Kana Minami

• Minori Chihara as Chiaki Minami

• Nana Mizuki as Tōma Minami

• Rika Morinaga as Makoto/Mako-chan

• Tetsuya Kakihara as Fujioka

• Daisuke Ono as Hosaka

• Aki Toyosaki as Yoshino

• Eri Kitamura as Yuka Uchida

• Momoko Ohara as Shūichi

• Saori Gotō as Keiko

• Ao Takahashi as Riko

• Yoshino Nanjō as Miyuki

• Tatsuya Hayama as Akira Minami

• Reiko Takagi as Maki

• Ryōko Ono as Atsuko

• Ayaka Saitō as Hitomi

• Saeko Chiba as Hayami

• Hiroyuki Yoshino as Natsuki Minami

• Shinji Kawada as Haruo Minami

• Shintarō Asanuma as Takeru

Jun'ichi Kitamura ( Catch Me at the Ballpark! , Fluffy Paradise ; episode director for Cells at Work! Code Black ) is directing the new anime at LIDEN FILMS . Takamitsu Kōno is returning from previous Minami-ke series to oversee the series scripts, Nobuhiro Andō ( Agents of the Four Seasons: Dance of Spring , Hell's Paradise , My Deer Friend Nokotan episode animation director) is designing the characters, Masaru Satō ( Case Closed: The Bride of Halloween , Case Closed: The Fist of Blue Sapphire films, Komi Can't Communicate ) and Midori Kikuchi ( Beheneko: The Elf-Girl's Cat is Secretly an S-Ranked Monster! assistant art director) are the art directors.

The other staff members include:

• Color Key Artist: Saki Kurata

• Compositing Director of Photography: Yūki Tsuchimoto

• Sound Director: Yasunori Ebina (returning)

• Sound Effects: Naoto Yamaya (returning)

• Music: Yasuhiro Misawa (returning)

The "Mixa Animation Diary ' Minami-ke ' 20th Anniversary Tanabata Festival" first announced the new Minami-ke anime in July 2024. Another event announced its "Korekara" subtitle in November 2025. The new anime will be the fifth television anime in the franchise , and the first new television anime in the franchise in at least 14 years, as the last anime series aired in 2013.

Sakuraba launched the ongoing Minami-ke manga in Kodansha 's Weekly Young Magazine in 2004. Kodansha published the manga's 29th compiled book volume on Friday.

The manga inspired four television anime in 2007, 2008, 2009, and 2013, as well as three OVAs in 2009, 2012, and 2013.

The franchise centers on the three sisters of the Minami household: Haruka, Kana, and Chiaki. They live an average life, but they only have each other to depend on.

Sakuraba's Kyo no Gononi manga similarly inspired an OVA in 2006 and a television anime in 2008, as well as a separate 2009 OVA .

title: Harajuku Himegoto House Multimedia Project Announced
content:
Animate announced on Saturday a new multimedia project titled Harajuku Himegoto House , which will include a television anime, music, and more.

The "high-tempo gag" story follows an aspiring hitman who heads to a rumored hideout for assassins in Harajuku, only to discover a cafe staffed by an eclectic group of high-fashion, eccentric individuals.

The project's cast includes:

• Yūya Hirose as Mizuki Otokozawa, an aspiring hitman

• Tetsuei Sumiya as Mero Togariishi, a high-tension positive "gal"

• Sōhei Horikane as Takara Rokurokusō, a foul-mouthed gothic lolita doll

• Masaru Yoshimura as Kentarō Jinbayama, a centaur who is the ideal man

• Takuma Nagatsuka as Yuki Inubo, a man who wants cure his blue mood

• Nobuhiko Okamoto as Hitoshi Haritsukekawara; the twin-tailed, 50-year-old, decora-fashionista store manager

• Showtaro Morikubo as Shō Dogenzaka, a flashy men who is 2 trillion yen (about US$12.6 billion) in debt

Plott is responsible for the project's planning and production, Bandai Namco Music Live ( Lantis ) is providing the project's music, and Animate is collaborating on promotion. Visual artist Aki Akane (also known as Akane Aki ) drafted the project's original character illustrations.

The project's first group song will debut on Sunday.

title: 3 Most Powerful Dragon Ball Techniques That No One Can Win Against
content:
Even several years after its debut, the legacy of Dragon Ball can’t be matched by any other anime or manga series. As a battle Shonen, the series has introduced several iconic techniques that add to the thrill of the story. Written and illustrated by Akira Toriyama, the manga revolutionized the Shonen demographic in many ways, and it still continues to inspire a new generation of creators. With a legacy spanning over four decades, the franchise has released several spin-offs, sequels, series, movies, video games, merchandise, and more. Among the many tropes introduced in the story, one of the best is still the energy attacks that use signature techniques and blend them with martial arts.

These attacks are often derived from ki, a life-force energy that all beings possess and can learn to control, and are the core of the series’ power system. The original manga, which began serialization in 1984, immediately established the concept of energy attacks and martial arts techniques and continues to follow it to this day. This trope only continued to evolve in the later series and sequels, including Dragon Ball Z and Dragon Ball Super . While each of them is unique and possesses special powers, these five may be impossible to win against.

3) Solar Flare

Solar Flare is yet another unique technique that can’t be categorized as offensive or defensive. Instead of inflicting direct damage to the user, this ability renders them immobile for a few seconds by compromising their vision. The user channels their ki to release a blinding flash of light that temporarily compromises the vision of everyone in the vicinity. It’s virtually impossible to fight against this technique since physical strength doesn’t offer any defense against light. This technique works best as a team effort in a strategy to outnumber the target. By temporarily immobilizing the opponent, the user can either directly charge towards them with another offensive attack or create an opening for their team member to weaken them further. While this technique doesn’t directly cause harm to the target, it might change the tide of the battle as long as the user times it correctly and forms a strategy around it.

2) Evil Containment Wave

This ability was first introduced in the original Dragon Ball anime, but never got the spotlight it deserved. Master Roshi learned it from his own master, and it became one of his most terrifying techniques. Rather than an offensive or defensive attack, Evil Containment Wave is merely a sealing technique that traps an immortal or an unimaginable power enemy inside a container. After trapping the opponent in a container or a jar, the user seals them with a special talisman. Mastering this technique allows the user to defeat an opponent several times more powerful than them. This technique is not only difficult to dodge, but unlike usual fights, the difference in strength doesn’t matter as long as the target can become eternally trapped. This technique was also reintroduced in Dragon Ball Super since it was the only way to stop Zamasu, but the only reason it failed was that Goku forgot to bring the sealing talisman with him.

1) Spirit Bomb

Spirit Bomb is one of the few techniques Goku learned from King Kai, and it’s easily one of the most powerful techniques in the entire verse. However, its efficiency depends on the number of living creatures contributing their powers for Goku to land one devastating attack. Goku can extract the energy from all kinds of living creatures, compiling them into a gigantic ball of energy. The only reason Goku can use this technique is that he has a pure heart, which is why he can manipulate and gather energy. However, this technique can’t be used by many people, which is a major reason why Goku has an advantage in many battles. Not only that, but the fact that it basically draws limitless energy from external sources guarantees that there’s no fixed limit to the devastation this ability can cause. During the final stretch of the battle against Buu, Goku gathered energy from all life forms on Earth and created a Super Spirit Bomb, which was so powerful that the villain couldn’t even find an opening to regenerate himself.

title: 5 Upcoming Comedy Anime Set to Make Winter 2027 Hilarious
content:
2027 is just around the corner, and with the new year comes a fresh lineup of anime . Almost every season this year has stood out in its own way, and it seems the next year is set to do the same. However, Winter 2027 is shaping up to be a particularly hilarious season.

Winter 2027 will feature five especially hilarious anime, four of which are action-comedies, while the remaining one is a slice-of-life romantic comedy with an equally hilarious premise. These are five anime that every fan should keep an eye on this winter for a good laugh.

5) Sakamoto Days Season 2

Amid the wave of action-comedy anime arriving next season, Netflix will bring back Sakamoto Days with its second season . The new season will continue the adventures of the titular character and his partner, Shin, as they venture into the JCC to uncover the identity of the intriguing villain who has brought chaos to Sakamoto’s peaceful life. The first season proved to be a uniquely entertaining shonen anime, blending the comedic premise of assassins with the main characters’ commitment to family in a surprisingly effective way.

What makes this anime stand out even more is its action, which is crafted in a distinctive way that seamlessly incorporates comedy, something not many other series can pull off. The second season aims to surpass the first in animation and other aspects, which is sure to elevate the anime’s action-comedy even further next season.

4) Marriagetoxin Season 2

Speaking of assassins with peculiar action sequences, Marriagetoxin also fits the bill, sometimes even more than others, thanks to its blend of romance and action. The series follows the protagonist, Hikaru, on his expedition to find a wife. However, that is easier said than done, as he knows nothing about dating but is an expert at killing using his poison specialties. The series sees him getting help from someone who eventually becomes his marriage advisor, guiding Hikaru through numerous dates as he explores the world of dating.

Hikaru’s interactions with several different women teach the poison master new aspects of romantic life, all while being elevated by awkward and comical situations. Meanwhile, the action is entirely different and becomes gripping whenever needed, fulfilling the series’ action-comedy appeal. Bones Film has also helped the anime look better than many others , making Marriagetoxin Season 2 a hilarious, top-quality action-comedy that fans shouldn’t miss.

3) One-Punch Man Season 3 Part 2

One-Punch Man is arguably one of the funniest action-comedy anime released in the last decade. Despite the anime’s trajectory potentially making it one of the most disappointing adaptations due to its poor animation quality since Season 2, it remains a hilarious series that fans can enjoy. The second part of One-Punch Man Season 3 will continue the events left unfinished in the previous part, covering the Monster Association arc, with the heroes gathering to take on the monsters as Garou continues to grow more powerful.

The previous part largely kept Saitama out of the action, but the upcoming episodes are set to feature him much more prominently. The teaser trailer already hilariously highlights Saitama and Sonic’s interaction, bringing back the comedy the series is known for through Saitama’s reactions to those around him and his concern over even the smallest things. If J.C. Staff manages to pull this off , especially with the biggest fights yet to come, nothing will stop One-Punch Man Season 3 Part 2 from emerging as one of 2027’s biggest action-comedy anime.

2) Mashle: Magic and Muscles Season 3

The last action-comedy series returning in Winter 2027 , which also has one of the most unique premises of all time, is Mashle: Magic and Muscles , coming back with its third season. The anime’s premise is unlike any other, blending the One-Punch Man vibe with the magical world of Harry Potter. The series follows an oddity who is deprived of magic but makes up for it with his muscles. The first two seasons featured all the classic shonen elements, including rivalries, bonds, and training, all elevated by Mash Burnedead’s peculiar ability to use his muscles for everything.

The latest season set up the Divine Visionary arc, which, towards the end, saw the villains infiltrating the academy in classic shonen fashion. The third season is set to continue this adventure, forcing Mash to showcase his muscular oddity even more amid the waves of magical challenges, making every fight funnier than ever among the anime of 2027.

1) The Guy She Was Interested In Wasn’t a Guy At All

As the title suggests, The Guy She Was Interested In Wasn’t a Guy At All is a yuri, or girls’ love, manga with one of the most hilarious premises ever. Adapted by CloverWorks from the manga of the same name, the anime will feature Aya, a girl with a particular taste in rock music who becomes attracted to the clerk at a CD shop. However, a surprising twist reveals that the clerk is actually a girl, who also happens to be Mitsuki, the classmate sitting next to her at school.

Mitsuki doesn’t tell Aya the truth because she enjoys the latter’s attention and the gossip she shares about the CD shop clerk. Sharing many similarities in their taste in music and other little nuances, The Guy She Was Interested In Wasn’t a Guy At All is shaping up to be a different kind of anime arriving in Winter 2027 . It could also be the most hilarious anime of the season, thanks to its intriguing premise, which adds variety and broadens the anime genre landscape.

title: Netflix’s One Piece Zoro Star Reveals He Spent 3 Years Preparing for an Anime Role Other Than Zoro
content:
Netflix’s One Piece Zoro star Mackenyu apparently built his body for a new anime role over the past three years. The Japanese actor has made a name for himself in anime live-action adaptations over the years by embodying several different roles. From villains and heroes to supporting characters, Mackenyu has proven to be the perfect actor for live-action adaptations. However, no role has earned him a reputation quite like Zoro, and there is little he could do to top it. While the first season saw him bringing Zoro to life, the second season took his portrayal to the next level, thanks to its action sequences and the physique the actor built for the role.

A still from the second season of the series reveals that Mackenyu has been putting in the work to make Zoro look more accurate. However, his latest anime role reveals that all this preparation was actually for a different character, as Mackenyu himself confirmed. It was recently revealed that a live-action movie adaptation of the underrated magical comedy series, Mashle: Magic and Muscles , is set to release on March 19, 2027 , with Mackenyu playing the role of Mash, for which he looks perfect. A detailed report shared by Oricon Japan following an interview reveals that this was no coincidence, as Mackenyu has been preparing for this role.

Mackenyu Has Been Preparing for His Next Anime Role for Three Years

In the interview shared by Oricon Japan , it was revealed that when the live-action adaptation of Mashle was greenlit, the series’ director, Yuichi Fukuda, offered Mackenyu the lead role of Mash Burnedead just five seconds after the announcement. While Mackenyu immediately expressed his excitement about landing the role, he then spent the next three years building muscle for the character. The interview also reveals that the director was concerned about potential filming conflicts with Mackenyu’s role as Zoro in One Piece . With two seasons already filmed over the past three years and the third season now wrapping up, Mackenyu likely only got to film the movie recently.

In the meantime, while portraying Zoro, it is evident that Mackenyu continued training and building muscle, developing the physique needed for his upcoming role as Mash in the live-action movie. Considering that he filmed the movie recently, possibly after One Piece Season 3, Mackenyu could look bigger and better than he did as Zoro in Netflix’s One Piece Season 2. Even the series’ original creator, Hajime Komoto, visited the set during filming, and his biggest highlight was seeing Mackenyu’s physique. Although the teaser released so far does not fully showcase the muscles Mackenyu has built for the role, his expressions and the first close-up reveal that he is perfect for the character.

While the past three years of preparation made it seem that Mackenyu was building his physique to portray Zoro more accurately, his latest remarks reveal that his main focus was actually Mash . In essence, fans got to see Mackenyu’s physique change drastically between the first and second seasons of Netflix’s One Piece as a side effect of his preparation for a new anime role. And the first look reveals that his new character could be an even more perfect fit than Zoro.

The interview also reveals that the director was concerned about potential filming conflicts with Mackenyu’s role as Zoro in One Piece . With two seasons already filmed over the past three years and the third season now wrapping up, Mackenyu likely only got to film the movie recently.

In the meantime, while portraying Zoro, it is evident that Mackenyu continued training and building muscle, developing the physique needed for his upcoming role as Mash in the live-action movie. Considering that he filmed the movie recently, possibly after One Piece Season 3, Mackenyu could look bigger and better than he did as Zoro in Netflix’s One Piece Season 2. Even the series’ original creator, Hajime Komoto, visited the set during filming, and his biggest highlight was seeing Mackenyu’s physique. Although the teaser released so far does not fully showcase the muscles Mackenyu has built for the role, his expressions and the first close-up reveal that he is perfect for the character.

While the past three years of preparation made it seem that Mackenyu was building his physique to portray Zoro more accurately, his latest remarks reveal that his main focus was actually Mash . In essence, fans got to see Mackenyu’s physique change drastically between the first and second seasons of Netflix’s One Piece as a side effect of his preparation for a new anime role. And the first look reveals that his new character could be an even more perfect fit than Zoro.

title: Dragon Ball’s Mid-Card Fighters Deserve More Screen Time
content:
The start of the Dragon Ball universe didn’t always feature power levels well out of the stratosphere, and in fact, the entire first original anime introduced fighters like Tien, Krillin, Master Roshi and more . Then the Super Saiyan power-up was introduced, and everyone quickly forgot this group of normal fighters. Dragon Ball Z attempted to add some fresh non-Saiyan faces into that roster with the likes of the Androids and Majin Buu, but they’ve fallen to the wayside in recent years, and it’s understandable why.

They’ve been surpassed by such a margin that it made little sense to keep track of their progress. At one time, however, most of those names were powerful fighters in Akira Toriyama’s universe. It’s worth exploring their progress as well, just like Gohan. His studies might’ve softened him up, but he proved that he still had elite ability in Dragon Ball Super: Super Hero . Now, he’s a Saiyan and obviously well above those other fighters, but as a group, they create a formidable fighting force. Maybe there’s a miniseries or movie they can find their niche in.

Dragon Ball Super Shows The Group Kept Training

All of the characters mentioned above, minus Buu who fell asleep, got to showcase their talents in Dragon Ball Super ‘s Tournament of Power . They each scored at least one elimination too, so there’s no doubt they could hold their own in some big-time battles. Furthermore, Android 17 won the final match of the tourney to clinch a victory for Universe 7. It’s unfortunate that a few of them fell out of the plot. Between Buu’s antics with Mr. Satan and his laziness when it comes to fights, and Krillin’s many defeats in the series, they’ve been relegated to comic relief.

Looking back at their performances over the course of the franchise, each one has their moments and abilities. The Androids boast super speed and pulverized the Z Fighters before joining them. Tien won the World Martial Arts Tournament in the original Dragon Ball by defeating Goku, albeit as a kid, but still an impressive win in any form. And who can forget how devastating and iconic his Tri Beam attack is, especially in his fight against Cell? Tien’s power demanded respect after that battle.

Krillin proved his worth in the Frieza saga, destroying the emperor’s tail with a Destructo Disc. He never won the fight, but he held his own until Goku arrived. Master Roshi taught Goku and Krillin in the first place, and he showed he still carried significant power. Although it’s probably best he use it sparingly after his death and resuscitation in his Dragon Ball Super tourney win.

Majin Buu Still Has a Lot of Potential as a Z Fighter

Last but certainly not least, Majin Buu might’ve fallen asleep when called upon, but his power is never to be questioned. Especially when he’s angry. His regeneration ability makes him maybe the most dangerous of the bunch. Obviously the Saiyans and Piccolo are the headliners of the Z Fighters, but seeing the human fighters and Buu put up a valiant effort and pick up wins is a lot of fun too.

These characters got more focus in the past before the scope of the fights got way too big, so maybe it’s time to dust off the old favorites as the series goes forward. They carry a unique story that can, at minimum, get its own one-off film. What do you think about a showcase of Dragon Ball’ s less powerful fighters? Let us know in the comments.

title: Solo Leveling Studio’s Next Big Anime Confirms Release Date With New Trailer – Watch
content:
Now that 2026 is approaching its end, the anime industry is getting ready for its upcoming releases for 2027, including a gorgeous anime from A-1 Pictures. This is the same studio behind Solo Leveling , and it’s known for several acclaimed shows. The studio’s latest project, Bless , is one of the most anticipated anime of 2027. It was already scheduled for the Winter 2027 lineup, and now that the season is closer than ever, the studio confirmed its release date in a new trailer. The gorgeous trailer sheds more light on the main characters before confirming that the anime will premiere on January 8th, 2027.

The official X handle of the anime also shared a key visual along with the confirmation that the episodes will broadcast every Friday at 11:30 P.M. on Fuji TV’s Noitamina network. The new trailer also introduces the cast and crew, along with a few new glimpses at the main characters. The anime has already gathered a lot of attention not only because of its visuals and unique premise, but also because the studio behind Solo Leveling is producing it, which is enough to pique fans’ interest. Established in 2005, this renowned studio is responsible for creating several modern classics such as Kaguya-sama: Love Is War , Your Lie in April , and many more.

Bless Will Be Streaming Globally on Crunchyroll

Last month, Crunchyroll confirmed acquiring the streaming rights to the anime , although the release schedule hasn’t been revealed yet. We can expect the episodes to drop on the platform around a couple of hours after the Japanese broadcast. The streaming platform has a lot of information to share regarding Bless , including the release time, the regional availability, and the English dub details. The English dub is usually released at least two weeks after the original premiere. Crunchyroll has yet to share its Winter 2027 schedule, which will include all the information regarding the upcoming anime series, including Bless . If the anime is confirmed for an English dub, the platform will also introduce the new cast and crew ahead of the dub’s debut.

Bless Is One of the Most Unique Shonen Series That You Can’t Miss

The anime is based on Yukino Sonoyama’s acclaimed Shonen manga, which began serialization in Kodansha’s monthly Shonen Sirius magazine in 2022. The story centers around 15-year-old Aia Udagawa , who has been chosen as a model for the Aoi Festival Artist Contest due to his previous experience. However, amid his inner struggles, he notices Jin Sumisaki, a tall and awkward girl who appears embarrassed about her appearance. The two of them are paired as a model and stylist, which becomes a major turning point in their lives. While Udagawa regrets abandoning his dream after convincing himself he has no talent, Sumisaki lacks the confidence to work as a model despite having the stunning features that make her stand out from the crowd. The story continues as the duo embraces their dreams while giving each other the push needed to break free from the shackles of self-doubt.

Are you excited for the anticipated premiere of Bless ? Head down to the comments to let us know about your expectations for the anime.

title: Avatar: Seven Havens Producers Debunk Major Timeskip Theory
content:
Avatar: Seven Havens has officially brought its first season to an end with Paramount+ , and the producers behind it all have unfortunately shut down any hopes of a big time skip coming anytime soon. When Avatar: Seven Havens was gearing up for its debut during a panel at New York Comic Con 2026 earlier this Fall, a piece of concept art showing off an older look for Pavi and Nisha had fans wondering whether or not that would be seen in the series itself as the result of a potential time skip.

Avatar: Seven Havens ended its first season with Pavi and Nisha separating as the two of them are now off on their own journeys , so fans had been wondering if it would lead to a time skip as Pavi visits each of the other Havens. Speaking to IGN , franchise co-creator Michael DiMartino and executive producers Sehaj Sethi and Ethan Spaulding reveal that there won’t be a lengthy time jump outside of accounting for travel time between Havens, “Time passes, but it’s not like we’re jumping forward years or anything.”

Don’t Expect a Big Timeskip in Avatar: Seven Havens

When asked about that piece of concept art itself that sparked all of these fan theories in the first place, Avatar: Seven Havens executive producer Sehaj Sethi shut down the idea with, “that was concept art. So whether there’s a time jump, who’s to say, but that was not a time jump piece of art. That was just concept art.” Executive producer Ethan Spaulding further explained that time will be passing between episodes as normal, and be more in line with how Avatar: The Last Airbender’ s own events played out .

“Within the span of a series, there’s time in between episodes,” Spaulding noted. “It’s not very big, but you could say they’re traveling for weeks or months. It’s similar to Last Airbender .” To which co-creator Michael DiMartino then put the final nail in the coffin with “Yeah, now that they’re on the road, [you] gotta account for the travel time in certain ways,” DiMartino stated. “Time passes, but it’s not like we’re jumping forward years or anything.” So there will be days and even months between events, but not going as far as featuring a much older version of the twins over its four seasons .

What Does This Mean for Avatar: Seven Havens ‘ Future?

Avatar: Seven Havens has been renewed through to Season 4, and the producers behind it have confirmed that the series will end its story with that fourth and final season. They have clearly mapped out everything that’s going to happen, and are currently far enough in production that if they say there isn’t going to be a big time skip, unfortunately it means there won’t be one. But there really won’t need to be one either way if the series does have a pace like Avatar: The Last Airbender.

That series is still held in high regard because of everything that happens in it, but looking back it only takes place within the span of a couple of years. Yet it never seemed like events were happening too quickly, and that was because the series was paced in such a way that it was able to do everything it needed to within that small pocket of time. It’s likely going to be the case for Pavi and Nisha’s journey too .

Do you want to see a time skip in Avatar: Seven Havens ‘ future? How are you liking the series after its first season? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!

HT – IGN

title: One Piece Made It Impossible to Ignore How Much the Creator Favors Sanji Over Zoro, And Fans Can’t Deny It
content:
Warning: This article contains spoilers from the One Piece manga! The debate regarding Zoro and Sanji’s powers may never be settled among fans, but One Piece ‘s creator has his own plans regarding the characters. As the Wings of the Pirate King, there’s no denying that Zoro and Sanji are not only Luffy’s most powerful allies, but they also have a huge role in the story. While Zoro is the first mate and a swordsman, Sanji is the cherished chef of the crew, on top of being an incredible fighter. Zoro and Sanji have been neck and neck with each other in terms of powers and their contribution to the story.

There’s no denying that Luffy needs both of them to become the pirate king . Even so, every fan has their favorite among these two, and the fan discourse often becomes as heated as their rivalry. However, after almost 30 years of serialization, it’s becoming evident that not only fans but even the creator, Eiichiro Oda, has a favorite among these two. Sanji is often considered one of the best-written characters in Shonen, and it’s all thanks to the effort Oda has put into him throughout these decades. Now that the Elbaph Arc is nearing its end, it’s more evident than ever that Oda has favored Sanji on multiple occasions.

Sanji’s Character Development Is the Best in One Piece & It’s Not Even Close

Sanji’s development happens over the decades, and it continues on even now. Ever since his introduction, he stood out as someone with strong morals. He was unapologetically kind, caring, and even goofy, which is why he immediately became a fan-favorite character. However, it didn’t take long for the story to reveal a part of his backstory when he met Zeff as a child and survived after being stranded on an island for weeks. This experience taught him the value of food, and he never spent a day wasting anything for the rest of his life. However, that tragic backstory only scratched the surface since Sanji’s life had been extremely difficult long before he came to the East Blue.

The story continues to feature his journey ever since his introduction in the Baratie Arc as he gets more powerful over the years. While the story also dropped subtle hints about his origins, especially in the Skypiea Arc when he mentioned he was from North Blue, the series didn’t give a concrete hint about his true past. It wasn’t until the Whole Cake Island Arc that the series revealed his origins and his horrible childhood when he suffered abuse from his family. Coming from a family of elite fighters who relied on genetic modifications, Sanji was discarded when he failed to meet his father’s expectations.

The trauma and struggles he faced during his childhood shaped him into the person he is today and guided his actions throughout his life. The arc was solely dedicated to him and his development, where he not only came to terms with his past but also completely broke ties with his family after saving them from Big Mom. Without the burden of his past, he reached new heights of power, especially after awakening his Germa 66 powers. The series has been progressing his story over the years, and every minor development comes together in the Elbaph Arc where he awakens his Conqueror’s Haki .

Sanji’s Conqueror’s Haki Awakening Has a Much Deeper Meaning Than Fans Realize

At this point, it’s pretty evident that Sanji’s Conqueror’s Haki is the result of his journey over the years . Sanji’s development doesn’t stop in the Whole Cake Island Arc when he severed ties with his family, but that was only the beginning of what we were going to see from him. Everything he faced in the Whole Cake Island Arc helped him overcome his past traumas and accept himself for who he is. Although he never showed it, he dealt with self-loathing and lack of self-worth. His self-sacrificial nature allowed him to even risk his life for his friends, but he would never want to rely on them. Even though he became stronger after escaping his family in childhood, the idea that he was worthless was deeply ingrained in Sanji’s mind, which led him to believe he shouldn’t ask others for help.

However, this all changed in the Wano Country Arc when he faced Black Maria, an opponent he could have easily defeated if she wasn’t a woman. Sanji would rather die than actually hit a woman, which is why he asked Robin for help. He not only trusted her abilities but also relied on her since he had nowhere to escape. This is a stark contrast compared to Enies Lobby when he couldn’t fight Kalifa and Nami had to interfere. He never asked her for help, but she decided to save him anyway. Not only that, but his experience on Ivankov’s island also taught him self-love, which was more important than any ordinary training.

He always had the potential to awaken his Conqueror’s Haki sooner if only he wasn’t held back by his own inner demons. In Chapter 1197, he finally overcame his long-standing self-loathing, which is the biggest reason he was able to tap into this power. The awakening seems even more meaningful because it is proof of his self-acceptance. He remembered Ivankov’s words and finally understood that the love he felt for his crew and those he cared about is worthless if he keeps treating himself as disposable. This is why his awakening is one of the most memorable moments in the series. His journey is far from over, and there’s no telling how much further he will go now that he has the one power he needed the most.

Zoro Never Got As Much Attention As Sanji in One Piece

There’s no denying that Zoro will always be one of the most beloved Shonen characters, but when it comes to character writing, he always falls behind Sanji. Not only does has one of the most underwhelming backstories in the series , but he never got an arc solely dedicated to him. Fans had high expectations for his character writing in Wano, but the series only glossed over his true lineage without revealing much about his past. It was so underwhelming that at this point, the story wouldn’t change much even if fans forget he belongs to a legendary noble clan of Wano. Regardless, the main issue lies with the fact that he mostly shines in battles, but the story of One Piece is so much more than just cool fights.

This is why Sanji has the upper hand since he draws fans in with his emotional story and themes of self-love and acceptance. We also can’t forget that Zoro’s Conqueror’s Haki awakening, which was an anticipated moment, is considerably underwhelming when compared to Sanji. Instead of featuring his development, the series rand3omly showed him knocking down some of Kaido’s men during a conflict, and that was it. For the first mate to awaken such a legendary power , there’s no excuse as to why this scene was so underwhelming. When compared to Sanji, Zoro’s awakening scene feels even less exciting, and the difference will be even more evident in the anime series.

What do you think about Sanji’s development over the years? Does he overshadow Zoro in terms of writing and character depth? Share your thoughts in the comments below.

He remembered Ivankov’s words and finally understood that the love he felt for his crew and those he cared about is worthless if he keeps treating himself as disposable. This is why his awakening is one of the most memorable moments in the series. His journey is far from over, and there’s no telling how much further he will go now that he has the one power he needed the most.
Zoro Never Got As Much Attention As Sanji in One Piece

There’s no denying that Zoro will always be one of the most beloved Shonen characters, but when it comes to character writing, he always falls behind Sanji. Not only does has one of the most underwhelming backstories in the series , but he never got an arc solely dedicated to him. Fans had high expectations for his character writing in Wano, but the series only glossed over his true lineage without revealing much about his past. It was so underwhelming that at this point, the story wouldn’t change much even if fans forget he belongs to a legendary noble clan of Wano. Regardless, the main issue lies with the fact that he mostly shines in battles, but the story of One Piece is so much more than just cool fights.

This is why Sanji has the upper hand since he draws fans in with his emotional story and themes of self-love and acceptance. We also can’t forget that Zoro’s Conqueror’s Haki awakening, which was an anticipated moment, is considerably underwhelming when compared to Sanji. Instead of featuring his development, the series rand3omly showed him knocking down some of Kaido’s men during a conflict, and that was it. For the first mate to awaken such a legendary power , there’s no excuse as to why this scene was so underwhelming. When compared to Sanji, Zoro’s awakening scene feels even less exciting, and the difference will be even more evident in the anime series.
What do you think about Sanji’s development over the years? Does he overshadow Zoro in terms of writing and character depth? Share your thoughts in the comments below.

title: Godzilla Minus Zero Star Breaks Down Her Character’s Big Change for Sequel [EXCLUSIVE]
content:
Godzilla Minus Zero is now tearing its way through theaters worldwide with one of the best box office openings for Toho’s long running franchise yet , and the star behind Noriko, Minami Hamabe, opened up to ComicBook about her character’s big change in the sequel film. Godzilla Minus One introduced Noriko to the franchise as someone who barely survived one of Godzilla’s initial attacks, only then to reveal she indeed was able to make it out of all of that alive in the end. But as revealed in the sequel, that came with some unexpected side effects.

Godzilla Minus Zero reveals that Noriko was able to survive the film thanks to the G Cells that had made it into her body, and she had subsequently mutated as a result. Speaking to ComicBook about this change in her character and her resulting link with Godzilla as a result, Hamabe explains that while Godzilla is positioned differently in this sequel due to this impact on Noriko and the arrival of a new threat , Noriko herself is still far from seeing the famous kaiju as a hero of some sort as it’s still a “symbol of fear in a lot of ways.”

Godzilla Minus Zero ‘s Noriko Talks G Cells and Link to Godzilla

“Noriko for me still sees Godzilla as this symbol of fear in a lot of ways,” Hamabe began. “It represents fear itself, and it’s threatening everything that the characters in post-war Japan are trying to rebuild.” Elaborating on this threat, Hamabe explained that while Noriko’s direct link to Godzilla changed her perspective on it, this is still far from seeing it with anything other than object fear , “So I think there’s still a very strong hatred towards Godzilla and what it represents in Minus Zero because Noriko and Godzilla now have this link, it certainly changes slightly, but I don’t think that means Noriko sees Godzilla in any positive light.”

Digging into it further, Hamabe then revealed just how complex of a situation it really is for Noriko, “And for audiences who are seeing it, I think you can kind of feel there’s a very complex feeling that Noriko has towards Godzilla whenever even the word or idea of Godzilla crosses her mind on screen.” Although there’s a new threat that makes Godzilla seems like the lesser of two evils, it’s still something that Noriko doesn’t want to call on even with her connection, “Especially because she understands with King Ghidorah in the mix now , Godzilla is positioned differently in the larger landscape. But all said, I think Godzilla is still something that Noriko doesn’t want to see at any moment.”

Will Godzilla Minus Zero Get a Sequel?

Although all of the promotional materials for Godzilla Minus Zero touted that there would not be a third film to cap off a trilogy, the final moments of the film are clearly setting up for the next phase of the story . Koichi and Noriko have since escaped the clutches of the United States government, and her direct connection with Godzilla and the G Cells makes her more important that ever before. Especially because it’s clear that the G Cells also won’t be keeping Noriko alive forever. There’s a time limit on it all.

It’s possible for this take on Godzilla to end here, but it also seems like there’s still much more to explore for both Koichi and Noriko as the two of them just want to live peaceful lives after everything their small family has been through. But would you want to see the Godzilla Minus franchise returning for a third film? What would you want to see go down in it? Let us know all of your thoughts about it in the comments!
